messages.subject: Meeting tomorrow 12-2, hybrid format
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies,
Our first meeting of the new quarter is tomorrow at noon. We'll have a hybrid format so you can join us in the Datalab classroom (360 Shields library) or via zoom (link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862)

We will discuss plans and topics for the quarter, then move into a group study session where folks with questions can get support from one of our expeRts.

Please remember that you can always get help by posting your questions to our discussion forum at https://d-rug.discourse.group

-Your cooRdinators

messages.subject: Fall 2023 D-RUG schedule + next week's reading
messages.subject_clean: Fall 2023 D-RUG schedule + next week's reading
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Hope your fall quarter is off to a good start! D-RUG will meet on Wednesdays from 12 - 2 pm in the Datalab classroom (360 Shields library) or via zoom (link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862). Check out our exciting list of workshops for the quarter at the end of this email + more information on what we do in D-RUG.

Kicking us off next week, we are going to read the Debugging chapter <https://adv-r.hadley.nz/debugging.html> from Advanced R and discuss as a group. We'll then transition to open work time where you can ask youR questions or work alongside other R users.

Looking forward to this quarter with you all!
Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators
________________________________________________________________
Please remember to post your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

Mini-workshop schedule:

Oct 11: Advanced R, Debugging Chapter <https://adv-r.hadley.nz/debugging.html>
Oct 18: Terra package - Elise
Oct 25: Stan - Wes
Nov 1: TBD
Nov 8: brms - Wes/Tara
Nov 15: Debugging tools - Elise
Nov 22: Thanksgiving break
Nov 29: Inla - Wes
Dec 6: TBD

messages.subject: D-RUG this Wednesday: raster to terra!
messages.subject_clean: D-RUG this Wednesday: raster to terra!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We will meet this Wednesday from 12 - 2 pm in the Datalab Classroom (360 Shields library) with a zoom option <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>. Elise will be running a mini-workshop on switching from the raster package to terra. Here's a description of what to expect:

The sp and rgdal packages are officially archived, and raster is not long for this world either. It’s time to learn terra, or at least enough of it to future proof your code (for now). Bring your own code for help transitioning it after the talk. You can find the GitHub repository for this workshop here: https://github.com/d-rug/raster_to_terra.

We'll transition to open work time after the workshop :)

See you then!

messages.subject: D-RUG this Wednesday: Ihaka lecture on interactive graphics
messages.subject_clean: D-RUG this Wednesday: Ihaka lecture on interactive graphics
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We will meet this Wednesday from 12 - 2 pm in the Datalab Classroom (360 Shields library) with a zoom option <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>.

We will be streaming a lecture on Interactive Graphics and Data Analysis <https://www.youtube.com/live/gggu4HVZETo?feature=share> from Anthony Unwin, who contributed to the development of the Interactive Graphics software! The lecture is part of the Ihaka Lecture Series <https://www.auckland.ac.nz/en/science/about-the-faculty/department-of-statistics/ihaka-lecture-series.html> put on by the University of Auckland, which covers a range of interesting data science topics. The lecture will last just over an hour and then we will transition into open work time.

See you then!
